project: The Formula of Becoming - Week 1 Day 4 - Full Cast

narrator.instructions: Speak only supplied narration in a warm, grounded, observant, quietly lyrical documentary delivery. Be clear, restrained, and unhurried. Do not perform character dialogue or add words.

dr-brooks.instructions: Speak only Dr. Camille Brooks's supplied words with calm, warm, intellectually demanding classroom authority. Let questions invite reflection rather than demand a correct answer. Do not add words.

malik.instructions: Speak only Malik's supplied words. He is precise, guarded, economical, and quietly warm when trust appears. Use a measured medium-low delivery and dry humor without adding words.

nia.instructions: Speak only Nia's supplied words. She is bright, expressive, curious, and playful, with a lively conversational pace. Slow slightly for human consequences. Do not add words.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: On Monday, Dr. Brooks closed the classroom door and asked everyone to put away their calculators.

utterances.speaker: dr-brooks
utterances.text: Today,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: she said,

utterances.speaker: dr-brooks
utterances.text: I want the answer nobody can compute for you. Why does mathematics matter?

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: The room went quiet in the special way classrooms do when a question becomes personal.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Students spoke about engineering, medicine, money, teaching, technology, and being the first in their families to pursue a technical degree.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: When Malik's turn came, he folded his hands on the desk.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: My father can repair almost anything,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: he said.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: Engines, roofs, appliances. But one unexpected bill can undo months of planning. I want to understand risk well enough to help families and businesses prepare without pretending every loss can be prevented.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: The answer came out more honest than he intended. He looked down after finishing.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia did not make a joke.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: When her turn came, she said,

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: My aunt runs a neighborhood tutoring program. Every year she has to prove the same thing to different people: that kids are learning, that the program matters, that the money should continue. I want to use math to make important things harder to ignore.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: After class, they walked down Eliza Moss Hall's broad staircase.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: You want to make risk visible,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia said.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: You want to make people visible.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: That sounded like the end of a movie trailer.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: I regret saying it.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Too late. I heard the music.
